solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: People of over fifty lack spryness in the end

indicators.note: over tells us to turn the little word of round so it reads backwards

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of each of the two words lack and spryness

explanation.surface: Older people, past fifty, are no longer as nimble as they were.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, one's family or people in general are called this, a plural noun matching People.

clue.text: Dictator cut precursor to Euro

indicators.note: cut means the dictator's name loses its final letter

parts.note: General Franco was the dictator of Spain

explanation.surface: A dictator slashes something that came before the European currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The French and Belgian currency unit was replaced by the euro in 2002, so it came before it.

clue.text: Mostly thick, large, clumsy and sluggish

indicators.note: clumsy suggests letters put together awkwardly, so they are rearranged
Mostly means the word thick is used without its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone described as dim, big, awkward and slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' turns thick into THIC; 'clumsy' then rearranges THIC with LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sluggish and being lethargic are synonyms: both mean slow and lacking energy.

clue.text: Sweet shop item that's solidified with maybe mint filling

indicators.note: filling means one word goes inside the other, like stuffing in a pastry

parts.note: something that has solidified has set, like a jelly
mint is one example of a herb

explanation.surface: A confectioner's treat that has hardened, perhaps with a minty centre.
explanation.walkthrough: SHERBET is a fizzy powdered sweet sold in British sweet shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet powder is a classic product sold by the jar in a British confectioner's shop.

clue.text: Old record company produces annoying noise and moves away from country

parts.note: EMI is a long-established British record label
a sound that grates is harsh and irritating

explanation.surface: A veteran record label makes an irritating din and relocates abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's homeland to settle in another nation.

clue.text: In The Queen Vic warms up grub

indicators.note: the Queen Vic is the pub in EastEnders, where Cockney speakers drop their initial H

parts.note: to heat something is to warm it up

explanation.surface: Somebody at a famous soap pub reheats some food.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen Vic is the pub in the BBC soap EastEnders, set in London's East End; Cockneys there drop the H, so HEATS is said 'EATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub and this word are both informal terms for food.

clue.text: The Creation in ridiculous cine epic

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests the letters are made absurd, so they are scrambled

explanation.surface: A film about the Creation featured in an absurd big-screen spectacular.
explanation.definitionFit: Incipience is the beginning of something, and the Creation is the very beginning of the world.

clue.text: Crowd wanting a couple of letters in word game

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so two letters are removed from the front of the game

parts.note: Scrabble is the board game of making words from letter tiles

explanation.surface: A group of people short of tiles for a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: The couple of letters is SC, taken from the start; the joke is that Scrabble is played with letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble is a disorderly crowd or mob.

clue.text: Toerag with time to dishonestly increase the price …

parts.note: to ramp is to push a price up artificially or fraudulently

explanation.surface: A scoundrel who, given time, will rip people off with inflated prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Toerag is British slang for a scruffy vagrant or a contemptible person, both senses matching a vagabond.

clue.text: … on account of bank in earnest

parts.note: since can mean because, or on account of
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: a seriously meant explanation involving a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 7-down, but the clues are independent; the pair suggests ending a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in earnest means doing it genuinely, an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Real gold in that case is on credit? Not quite

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
then can mean in that case, as in 'then we'll go'

indicators.note: Not quite means the word is cut short by one letter at its end

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Is real gold, in that case, bought on credit? Not entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something genuine is real; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Meat dish, uncooked, put in empty basin

indicators.note: put in means one piece is placed inside the other
empty means the word basin loses its contents, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: raw food is uncooked

explanation.surface: A meat recipe, still raw, placed in a bowl that has been emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: Brawn is a British dish of meat from a pig's head set in jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawn is a cold, jellied preparation of pork, so it is a type of meat dish.

clue.text: Awkward call about a pair of bachelors

indicators.note: about means the call goes around the other letters

parts.note: to cry is to call out
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, so two of them gives BB

explanation.surface: An awkward shout concerning two unmarried men.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward here means bad-tempered or difficult, a meaning crabby shares as an adjective.

clue.text: See 18
This man will start to shoot canines etc — good grief

parts.note: he'll is the contraction of he will, said of this man

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of shoot

parts.note: canines, molars and incisors are teeth

explanation.surface: Someone about to fire at dogs and other animals, to general dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canines' looks like dogs, but here they are teeth. The exclamation is an old-fashioned British oath.
explanation.definitionFit: This old-fashioned British oath is an exclamation of surprise or dismay, much as good grief is.

clue.text: Met the girl in a rave — it shows the exposure you can get

definitions.text: it shows the exposure you can get

indicators.note: in a rave suggests letters dancing wildly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone met a girl at a dance party and gained some publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers use this device to measure light and so find the correct camera exposure.

clue.text: He scans speech 20's writing about international public relations

indicators.note: about means the editorial piece surrounds the other letters

parts.note: an editor (the answer to 20-down) writes the leader, the newspaper's opinion column

explanation.surface: An editor's column about global public relations, reviewed by someone reading a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person may follow speech by watching mouths move, scanning the speaker's lips.

clue.text: In bed maybe edges across between the covers

indicators.note: between the covers means only the inside letters are kept, the outer ones discarded

parts.note: to sidle is to edge sideways across a space

explanation.surface: Someone in bed shuffles over beneath the duvet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Between the covers' sounds like being in bed, but it removes the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in bed is one example of being inactive or doing nothing.

clue.text: Chap tried in error is almost free

indicators.note: in error suggests the letters are set down wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man wrongly put on trial is nearly released.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very cheap costs next to nothing, so it is almost free.

clue.text: Initially place ace around king, and all the rest

indicators.note: Initially means the first letter of place

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
C, for circa, means around
K is the card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A card player sets the ace beside the king, with the remaining cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Being one of the pack means being like all the others; the pack is the rest of the crowd.

clue.text: With 12, it's cooked up by high-tech companies with spies having cover blown

parts.note: BlackBerry made smartphones
Apple makes computers and phones

indicators.note: having cover blown means the outer letters of spies are lost, leaving the inside

explanation.surface: Something devised by technology firms whose secret agents have been exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit pie is baked in the oven, so it is literally cooked up.

clue.text: Black feller, one with online diary

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a logger fells trees

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned man who keeps an internet journal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' looks like slang for a man, but it is one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes a web log keeps a diary on the internet.

clue.text: What you're looking for cantered round and round — the hacks are beneath him

indicators.note: the second round means the turned word goes around the other piece
the first round means the word for cantered is turned back to front

parts.note: to canter is to ride, so cantered means rode
the thing a solver seeks is it, the answer itself

explanation.surface: A rider circling a track on horses, the hacks beneath him.
explanation.walkthrough: Hacks are both horses and journalists; the editor is above the hacks in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists, called hacks, report to the person in charge of the newspaper, who ranks above them.

clue.text: Former streetwalker shortly to have sex with European. Hurry up!

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner
ped is short for pedestrian, someone walking in the street
it is a familiar crossword term for sex

explanation.surface: A former prostitute urges a European client to be quick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streetwalker' suggests a prostitute, but here it is just a pedestrian.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite something is to speed it up, an imperative synonym for hurry up.

clue.text: It's milky white but could be paler

indicators.note: could be hints the letters might form a different word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Something milky white might still become lighter.
explanation.definitionFit: This gem, and the colour named after it, has a lustrous milky white sheen.

clue.text: Striker say in game of football?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, sounding like another

parts.note: one who socks, or hits, someone is a socker

explanation.surface: A goal-scoring forward playing a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer, but here it is someone who socks, or punches.
explanation.definitionFit: Association football is known by this name, especially in America; the question mark admits a playful definition.

clue.text: Flowing river with no force creating diversion

indicators.note: with no means the force letter is taken out

parts.note: something funny diverts or amuses people
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: A river, lacking power, is being diverted from its course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diversion' suggests rerouting a river, but it means amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid that is runny flows easily.

clue.text: Seaweed caught in snorkel pipe

indicators.note: caught in means the letters are held inside the words snorkel pipe

explanation.surface: A diver finds seaweed stuck in their breathing tube.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large brown seaweed that grows in underwater forests.

clue.text: Mortimer's last to appear in silly sketch

indicators.note: to appear in means one letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: daft means silly

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of Mortimer's name

explanation.surface: John Mortimer's last role is in a comic sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft and a sketch are both a rough first outline of a plan or drawing.

clue.text: Ivy for instance, always the ingénue

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
an ingénue is innocent and inexperienced, which is to be green

explanation.surface: Ivy is cast forever as the naive young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ivy' looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy keeps its leaves all year, so it is one example of a plant of that kind.

clue.text: Joint on straight drawer's in the monarch's office

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means the joint comes after the other piece

parts.note: a ruler is an instrument for drawing straight lines
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A joint on a straight line drawn in the king's study.
explanation.definitionFit: Rulership is the position of governing, which is the office held by a monarch.

clue.text: Come back and do steady work again?

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to ply a trade is to work at it steadily

explanation.surface: Should someone return and resume their regular job?
explanation.definitionFit: To come back can mean to answer or retort, a sense this verb shares.
